# spacyr: an R wrapper for spaCy

[![CRAN
Version](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/spacyr)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=spacyr)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/quanteda/spacyr/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/quanteda/spacyr/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Codecov test
coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/quanteda/spacyr/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/quanteda/spacyr?branch=main)
[![Downloads](https://cranlogs.r-pkg.org/badges/spacyr)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=spacyr)
[![Total
Downloads](https://cranlogs.r-pkg.org/badges/grand-total/spacyr?color=orange)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=spacyr)

An R wrapper to the spaCy “industrial strength natural language
processing” Python library from <https://spacy.io>.

## Installing the package

1.  Install the **spacyr** R package:

    - From CRAN:

    \
    [`install.packages`](https://rdrr.io/r/utils/install.packages.html)`(``"spacyr"``)`

    - From GitHub:

      To install the development version, run the following.

    \
    `# install.packages("pak")`\
    `pak``::`[`pak`](https://pak.r-lib.org/reference/pak.html)`(``"quanteda/spacyr"``)`

2.  Install spaCy and requirements

    Simply run:

    \
    [`library`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/library.html)`(`[`spacyr`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io)`)`\
    [`spacy_install`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_install.md)`(``)`

    This installs the latest version of spaCy. To install a specific
    version, give its number:

    \
    [`spacy_install`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_install.md)`(``version ``=`` ``"3.8.7"``)`

    `version` can also name one of spaCy’s optional sets of extra
    dependencies, such as `"apple"`, which makes spaCy faster on Macs
    with Apple silicon:

    \
    [`spacy_install`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_install.md)`(``version ``=`` ``"apple"``)`

    The install tool on <https://spacy.io/usage> shows the versions and
    extras that are available.

3.  (optional) Add more language models

    If left unchanged,
    [`spacy_install()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_install.md)
    adds the default “en_core_web_sm” model. You can add more language
    models with
    [`spacy_download_langmodel()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_download_langmodel.md).
    For instance, to install a small and efficient German language
    model:

    \
    [`spacy_download_langmodel`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_download_langmodel.md)`(``"de_core_news_sm"``)`

    Check out available models at <https://spacy.io/usage/models>.

    You can check whether spaCy and a model are ready to use, without
    starting Python, with:

    \
    [`spacy_installed`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_installed.md)`(``"en_core_web_sm"``)`

[`spacy_install()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_install.md)
creates its environment with a version of Python supported by the spaCy
release being installed, and offers to install one through
[`reticulate::install_python()`](https://rstudio.github.io/reticulate/reference/install_python.html)
if none is found. On Windows, `install_python()` requires
[git](https://git-scm.com/downloads/) to be installed and on your
`PATH`.

If you run into any problems, you can try the manual installation path
described below.

### Using Docker

See [Using spacyr with
Docker](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/articles/docker.html) for a
Dockerfile that installs spaCy and its language model during the build.

### Changing the Python version

An existing environment keeps the version of Python it was created with.
If that version is too old or too new for the spaCy release you want,
[`spacy_install()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_install.md)
stops with an error. To recreate the environment with a suitable Python,
remove it and install again:

\
[`spacy_uninstall`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_uninstall.md)`(``)`\
[`spacy_install`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_install.md)`(``)`

To use a particular Python, create the environment yourself first (see
step 2 of the manual installation below), then run
[`spacy_install()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_install.md).

### Using an existing Python or conda environment

If you already have a Python environment with spaCy installed, for
instance a conda environment, point **spacyr** to its Python executable
through the `RETICULATE_PYTHON` environment variable before calling
[`spacy_initialize()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_initialize.md):

\
[`Sys.setenv`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/Sys.setenv.html)`(``RETICULATE_PYTHON ``=`` ``reticulate``::`[`conda_python`](https://rstudio.github.io/reticulate/reference/conda-tools.html)`(``"my-spacy-env"``)``)`\
[`spacy_initialize`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_initialize.md)`(``model ``=`` ``"en_core_web_sm"``)`

You can also set `RETICULATE_PYTHON` in your `.Renviron` file. When it
is set, **spacyr** uses that Python instead of its own environment.

### Using local or custom language models

Besides the names of installed models,
[`spacy_initialize()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_initialize.md)
accepts the path to a model directory, for instance a model you have
trained or downloaded yourself:

\
[`spacy_initialize`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_initialize.md)`(``model ``=`` ``"path/to/my_model"``)`

### Manual installation and troubleshooting

[`spacy_install()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_install.md)
performs a number of tasks to set up a virtual environment in which
spaCy is installed. Virtual environments are the recommended way to
install Python applications, as the lack of central dependency conflict
control (which is performed by CRAN in the `R`-world) means that
conflicts between packages are a lot more common. Hence each Python
package and its dependencies are usually installed in their own folder.

Usually, none of this should concern you. However, experience shows that
some systems run into problems during installation that are hard to
foresee by developers. Below, we therefore explain how you can perform
the steps in
[`spacy_install()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_install.md)
manually, to debug any problems that might occur. Please only file a
GitHub issue after you have tried to manually run through the steps, so
we can provide you with more targeted help.

1.  Install Python

    You can use your own installation of Python for the steps below. By
    default,
    [`spacy_install()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_install.md)
    downloads and installs a minimal Python version in the default
    directory used by the `reticulate` package for simplicity. This can
    be done with a single command:

    \
    `python_exe`` ``<-`` ``reticulate``::`[`install_python`](https://rstudio.github.io/reticulate/reference/install_python.html)`(``)`

    The function returns the path to the Python executable file. You can
    run this again at any time to get that path (the installation is
    skipped if the files are already present).

    Without a `version`, this installs the default version of Python of
    the **reticulate** package, which may not be one that spaCy
    supports: each spaCy release works with a range of Python versions,
    shown as “Requires: Python” on its [PyPI
    page](https://pypi.org/project/spacy/).
    [`spacy_install()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_install.md)
    checks this for you; when installing manually, name a supported
    version if the default is not one:

    \
    `python_exe`` ``<-`` ``reticulate``::`[`install_python`](https://rstudio.github.io/reticulate/reference/install_python.html)`(``version ``=`` ``"3.12:latest"``)`

2.  Set up a virtual environment

    By default, `spacyr` uses an environment called “r-spacyr”, which is
    located in a directory managed by `reticulate`. We can create it
    with:

    \
    `reticulate``::`[`virtualenv_create`](https://rstudio.github.io/reticulate/reference/virtualenv-tools.html)`(``"r-spacyr"``, python ``=`` ``python_exe``)`

    If this causes trouble for some reason, you can install the
    environment in any location that is convenient for you like so:

    \
    `reticulate``::`[`virtualenv_create`](https://rstudio.github.io/reticulate/reference/virtualenv-tools.html)`(``"path/to/directory"``, python ``=`` ``python_exe``)`

    Note, that `spacyr` does not know of the existence of this
    environment unless you tell it through the environment variable
    `SPACY_PYTHON`. You can do that either in each session with:

    \
    [`Sys.setenv`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/Sys.setenv.html)`(``SPACY_PYTHON ``=`` ``"path/to/directory"``)`

    or you put it into your `.Renviron` file. You can use this little
    helper function to make the change permanent:

    \
    `usethis``::`[`edit_r_environ`](https://usethis.r-lib.org/reference/edit.html)`(``scope ``=`` ``"user"``)`

    We also need to tell `reticulate` that it should use this
    environment from now on.

    \
    `reticulate``::`[`use_virtualenv`](https://rstudio.github.io/reticulate/reference/use_python.html)`(`[`Sys.getenv`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/Sys.getenv.html)`(``"SPACY_PYTHON"``, unset ``=`` ``"r-spacyr"``)``)`

    We use `Sys.getenv("SPACY_PYTHON", unset = "r-spacyr")` to check if
    `SPACY_PYTHON` is set and use the default otherwise.

3.  Install spaCy

    Installing `spaCy` and its dependencies is again done through
    `reticulate`. We check again if SPACY_PYTHON is set, in case you
    chose a non-default folder.

    \
    `reticulate``::`[`py_install`](https://rstudio.github.io/reticulate/reference/py_install.html)`(``"spacy"``, envname ``=`` `[`Sys.getenv`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/Sys.getenv.html)`(``"SPACY_PYTHON"``, unset ``=`` ``"r-spacyr"``)``)`

4.  Install spaCy language models

    The language models are not available through `pip` by name, so they
    are installed with spaCy’s own download command, which
    [`spacy_download_langmodel()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_download_langmodel.md)
    runs for you:

    \
    `spacyr``::`[`spacy_download_langmodel`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_download_langmodel.md)`(``"en_core_web_sm"``)`

If any of those steps fail, please file an
[issue](https://github.com/quanteda/spacyr/issues) (after checking if
one already exists for your error). You can also use the individual
commands to customise your setup.

# Package index

## All functions

- [`as.dictionary(`*`<spacyr_entity_patterns>`*`)`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/as.dictionary.spacyr_entity_patterns.md)
  : Convert entity patterns of phrases to a quanteda dictionary
- [`as_entity_patterns()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/as_entity_patterns.md)
  : Create patterns for rule-based named entities
- [`as_index()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/as_index.md) :
  Convert matches, entities or noun phrases to a quanteda index
- [`data_char_paragraph`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/data_char_paragraph.md)
  : A short paragraph of text for testing
- [`data_char_sentences`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/data_char_sentences.md)
  : Sample short documents for testing
- [`entity_extract()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/entity_extract.md)
  [`entity_consolidate()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/entity_extract.md)
  : Extract or consolidate entities from parsed documents
- [`entity_patterns_read()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/entity_patterns_read.md)
  [`entity_patterns_write()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/entity_patterns_read.md)
  : Read and write entity patterns
- [`nounphrase_extract()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/nounphrase_extract.md)
  [`nounphrase_consolidate()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/nounphrase_extract.md)
  : Extract or consolidate noun phrases from parsed documents
- [`as.tokens(`*`<spacyr_parsed>`*`)`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/quanteda-methods.md)
  [`docnames(`*`<spacyr_parsed>`*`)`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/quanteda-methods.md)
  [`ndoc(`*`<spacyr_parsed>`*`)`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/quanteda-methods.md)
  [`ntoken(`*`<spacyr_parsed>`*`)`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/quanteda-methods.md)
  [`ntype(`*`<spacyr_parsed>`*`)`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/quanteda-methods.md)
  [`nsentence(`*`<spacyr_parsed>`*`)`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/quanteda-methods.md)
  : quanteda methods for parsed texts
- [`spacy_download_langmodel()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_download_langmodel.md)
  : Download spaCy language models
- [`spacy_download_langmodel_virtualenv()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_download_langmodel_virtualenv.md)
  : Install a language model in a conda or virtual environment
- [`spacy_extract_entity()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_extract_entity.md)
  : Extract named entities from texts using spaCy
- [`spacy_extract_nounphrases()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_extract_nounphrases.md)
  : Extract noun phrases from texts using spaCy
- [`spacy_finalize()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_finalize.md)
  : Finalize spaCy
- [`spacy_initialize()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_initialize.md)
  : Initialize spaCy
- [`spacy_install()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_install.md)
  : Install spaCy in a virtual environment
- [`spacy_install_virtualenv()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_install_virtualenv.md)
  : Install spaCy to a virtual environment
- [`spacy_installed()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_installed.md)
  : Check whether spaCy is installed
- [`spacy_match()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_match.md)
  : Match patterns in texts using spaCy
- [`spacy_parse()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_parse.md)
  : Parse a text using spaCy
- [`spacy_tokenize()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_tokenize.md)
  : Tokenize text with spaCy
- [`spacy_uninstall()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_uninstall.md)
  : Uninstall the spaCy environment
- [`spacy_upgrade()`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacy_upgrade.md)
  : Shorthand function to upgrade spaCy
- [`spacyr`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacyr-package.md)
  [`spacyr-package`](https://spacyr.quanteda.io/reference/spacyr-package.md)
  : An R wrapper to the spaCy NLP system
